evidence.claim: The IMF summarized the new policy model as relying on low interest rates, directing lending to selected sectors, and increasingly distortionary macrofinancial and regulatory measures; it also said inflation reached 85% in October 2022 and fiscal risks were rising.
evidence.title: Republic of Turkiye: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The IMF summarized the new policy model as relying on low interest rates, directing lending to selected sectors, and increasingly distortionary macrofinancial and regulatory measures; it also said inflation reached 85% in October 2022 and fiscal risks were rising.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF country report with a concise synthesis of the 2022 policy model, its consequences, and associated risks.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but still about the 2022 consultation and 2022 outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdogan because the low-rate model, directed credit, and intervention-heavy response were core government choices.
contrary_evidence: The same summary notes the public-debt burden remained low compared with peers.

evidence.claim: Erdogan vowed that the central bank would continue to cut policy rates every month as long as he remained in power.
evidence.title: Turkey's Erdogan says he will keep cutting rates "as long as I am in power"
evidence.excerpt: Erdogan vowed that the central bank would continue to cut policy rates every month as long as he remained in power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with a direct ruler quote and clear temporal fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler attribution because it is Erdogan's own commitment about economic policy.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes that inflation had surged and the lira had slumped after earlier cuts.

evidence.claim: Erdogan picked Nureddin Nebati to oversee and articulate the low-rate economic policy, and Reuters described him as having little direct economic training and as close to Erdogan's son-in-law Berat Albayrak.
evidence.title: Turkey's new finance minister in the eye of a storm
evidence.excerpt: Erdogan picked Nureddin Nebati to oversee and articulate the low-rate economic policy, and Reuters described him as having little direct economic training and as close to Erdogan's son-in-law Berat Albayrak.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a cabinet appointment with a clear loyalty and competence angle.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to the ruler-period economic team.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong attribution to Erdogan because the appointment was his and it fit the broader inner-circle economic lineup.
contrary_evidence: An AKP official in the same story said Nebati worked closely with the president and had stemmed the lira collapse.

evidence.claim: The 2022 annual program set macroeconomic, fiscal and sectoral policies and said the implementation measures would be concrete, measurable, limited to one year, and reviewed quarterly.
evidence.title: 2022 Yılı Cumhurbaşkanlığı Yıllık Programı 25/10/2021 Tarih ve 31639 (Mükerrer) Sayılı Resmi Gazete’de yayımlanmıştır
evidence.publisher: T.C. Cumhurbaşkanlığı Strateji ve Bütçe Başkanlığı
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 annual program set macroeconomic, fiscal and sectoral policies and said the implementation measures would be concrete, measurable, limited to one year, and reviewed quarterly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government program page; strong for formal priorities and implementation design, but not proof of execution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's presidential system and cabinet chain, though day-to-day implementation ran through ministries and agencies.
contrary_evidence: A written program is not evidence of effective delivery.
Later macro outcomes show mixed or weak implementation.

evidence.claim: OECD said central-bank interventions and administrative measures, including requiring exporters to convert 40% of foreign-currency revenue into lira and the exchange-rate protection scheme for lira deposits, helped stabilize the exchange rate in early 2022, while fiscal policy remained supportive through wage increases and energy-consumer support.
evidence.title: Türkiye: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2022 Issue 1
evidence.excerpt: OECD said central-bank interventions and administrative measures, including requiring exporters to convert 40% of foreign-currency revenue into lira and the exchange-rate protection scheme for lira deposits, helped stabilize the exchange rate in early 2022, while fiscal policy remained supportive through wage increases and energy-consumer support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent OECD surveillance with concrete policy detail and near-real-time assessment of implementation effects.
evidence.period_fit: Covers early 2022 implementation and market stabilization.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's policy line and the Treasury/central-bank apparatus under his control, though temporary stabilization also reflects coercive administrative tools and market conditions.
contrary_evidence: The OECD notes exchange-rate weakness later returned.
The measures can stabilize markets without solving underlying inflation.

evidence.claim: TURKSTAT reported that annual GDP increased by 5.5 percent in 2022, GDP per capita reached 10,659 dollars, exports of goods and services rose 9.9 percent, and imports rose 8.6 percent.
evidence.title: Annual Gross Domestic Product - 2022
evidence.excerpt: TURKSTAT reported that annual GDP increased by 5.5 percent in 2022, GDP per capita reached 10,659 dollars, exports of goods and services rose 9.9 percent, and imports rose 8.6 percent.
evidence.source_locator: press release summary on the data portal
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistical release from the national statistics office; strong for output and trade-growth outcomes, though not causal attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable in part to Erdoğan's policy setting, but also to tourism recovery, external demand, and base effects.
contrary_evidence: High nominal growth coexisted with severe inflation and exchange-rate depreciation.
GDP averages can mask household-level strain.

evidence.claim: In Madrid, Erdoğan and the Finnish and Swedish leaders agreed a trilateral memorandum addressing Türkiye's legitimate security concerns and paving the way for Finland and Sweden's NATO membership.
evidence.title: Türkiye, Finland, and Sweden sign agreement paving the way for Finnish and Swedish NATO membership
evidence.excerpt: In Madrid, Erdoğan and the Finnish and Swedish leaders agreed a trilateral memorandum addressing Türkiye's legitimate security concerns and paving the way for Finland and Sweden's NATO membership.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary NATO record of the agreement; strong evidence of diplomatic mobilization and concrete bargaining outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdoğan as Turkey's chief executive and foreign-policy decision-maker, though the final deal required counterparties and NATO facilitation.
contrary_evidence: The agreement depended on multilateral bargaining, not unilateral Turkish control.
It opened a process rather than completing accession that year.

evidence.claim: NATO said the Sweden-Finland accession process was the fastest in NATO's modern history and that Sweden was taking major concrete steps to implement the trilateral memorandum, including ending arms-sale restrictions and deepening counter-terrorism cooperation.
evidence.title: Press conference
evidence.excerpt: NATO said the Sweden-Finland accession process was the fastest in NATO's modern history and that Sweden was taking major concrete steps to implement the trilateral memorandum, including ending arms-sale restrictions and deepening counter-terrorism cooperation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: NATO transcript plus contemporaneous summary; strong evidence that the June bargain translated into follow-through during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Erdoğan's bargaining and Türkiye's leverage, though the concrete follow-through also depended on Sweden, Finland and NATO procedures.
contrary_evidence: The snippet reflects NATO's framing rather than Turkish self-report.
The process was still incomplete in 2022, so this is progress rather than completion.

evidence.claim: The UN said representatives from Ukraine, Russia and Türkiye signed an initiative in Istanbul that established a mechanism and a Joint Coordination Centre to safely transport grain, foodstuffs and fertilizer from Ukrainian ports to global markets and to prevent global hunger.
evidence.title: Note to correspondents on today’s agreements Istanbul
evidence.excerpt: The UN said representatives from Ukraine, Russia and Türkiye signed an initiative in Istanbul that established a mechanism and a Joint Coordination Centre to safely transport grain, foodstuffs and fertilizer from Ukrainian ports to global markets and to prevent global hunger.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN description of the agreement, mechanism and purpose; strong evidence of diplomatic execution and crisis management.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Erdoğan and the Turkish government as hosts and brokers, though success required Russian, Ukrainian and UN participation.
contrary_evidence: This was a multilateral arrangement, not a unilateral Turkish achievement.
Its success was contingent on war-time compliance and shipping security.

evidence.claim: By 12 September 2022, 2.7 million metric tons of grain and other foodstuffs had moved through the Black Sea Grain Initiative, and the Joint Coordination Centre in Istanbul was monitoring vessel movements and revising corridor procedures.
evidence.title: 2.7 million metric tons of grain and other foodstuffs were moved from Ukraine under Black Sea Grain Initiative
evidence.excerpt: By 12 September 2022, 2.7 million metric tons of grain and other foodstuffs had moved through the Black Sea Grain Initiative, and the Joint Coordination Centre in Istanbul was monitoring vessel movements and revising corridor procedures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN progress report with a concrete throughput figure and operational details; strong evidence of implementation and early results.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and only weeks after the agreement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable in part to Erdoğan's successful brokering and Türkiye's hosting of the JCC, though the throughput depended on all signatories and shipping compliance.
contrary_evidence: The initiative was not solely Turkish-owned.
Its durability depended on continuing wartime cooperation.

evidence.claim: The 2022 budget law amendment added 880.474775 billion TL in appropriations and increased the 2022 general-budget revenue estimate by 1.080515421 trillion TL.
evidence.title: 2022 Yılı Merkezi Yönetim Bütçe Kanunu ile Bağlı Cetvellerinde Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Kanun
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 budget law amendment added 880.474775 billion TL in appropriations and increased the 2022 general-budget revenue estimate by 1.080515421 trillion TL.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary legislative text with exact amounts and formal enactment record; strong evidence of a material mid-year budget revision.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022; the law was enacted mid-year to govern 2022 execution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutionally attributable to Erdoğan's presidential executive, since the law was proposed through the executive and signed into force, but the mechanics were parliamentary and budgetary rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: A budget revision shows adjustment, not successful delivery.
The law does not itself prove that all added funds were effectively spent.

evidence.claim: The parliamentary debate on the 2022 supplementary budget said the added funds were concentrated in public-sector wages, pensions and transfers, household energy support, infrastructure and investment, local governments, agriculture, and KKM-related costs.
evidence.title: 2022 Yılı Merkezi Yönetim Bütçe Kanunu ile Bağlı Cetvellerinde Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Kanun Teklifi münasebetiyle
evidence.excerpt: The parliamentary debate on the 2022 supplementary budget said the added funds were concentrated in public-sector wages, pensions and transfers, household energy support, infrastructure and investment, local governments, agriculture, and KKM-related costs.
evidence.source_locator: general assembly speech excerpt in the transcript
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary parliamentary transcript, but it is political speech and therefore self-justifying; useful for the allocation pattern, not as independent verification of outcomes.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to the supplementary budget debate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Erdoğan-led executive budget agenda; the allocation choices reflect government priorities, though not necessarily implementation quality.
contrary_evidence: Speech is a defense of the bill, not an audit.
The cited categories could still conceal inefficiencies or offsetting inflation effects.

evidence.claim: The year-end 2022 central budget closed with 2.802355 trillion TL of revenue, 2.941420 trillion TL of expenditure, and a 139.065 billion TL deficit.
evidence.title: 2022 Aralık Ayı Bütçe Gerçekleşme Sonuçları
evidence.excerpt: The year-end 2022 central budget closed with 2.802355 trillion TL of revenue, 2.941420 trillion TL of expenditure, and a 139.065 billion TL deficit.
evidence.source_locator: budget balance table in the page snippet
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct year-end finance ministry budget report with exact realized figures; strong for outcome and execution tracing.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the full 2022 budget year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Erdoğan-led fiscal program and Treasury administration, while inflation and exchange-rate conditions also affected nominal totals.
contrary_evidence: Nominal totals are inflated by price level changes.
The figures show budget execution, not whether spending was efficient or well-targeted.

evidence.claim: The finance ministry said that in 2022 the YBS reporting system was opened to spending units and allowed them to view budget, revenue, expenditure, balance-sheet and other accounting reports online.
evidence.title: Yönetim Bilgi Sistemi (YBS) Muhasebe Raporlama Platformu
evidence.publisher: T.C. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı Muhasebat Genel Müdürlüğü
evidence.excerpt: The finance ministry said that in 2022 the YBS reporting system was opened to spending units and allowed them to view budget, revenue, expenditure, balance-sheet and other accounting reports online.
evidence.source_locator: paragraph describing rollout to 'harcama birimleri' and report types
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary administrative notice showing a concrete reporting/monitoring tool deployment; strong for management capacity, weaker for proof of better outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutionally attributable to the Erdoğan-led finance apparatus as a management and monitoring improvement, but it is still a tooling rollout rather than outcome evidence.
contrary_evidence: A reporting platform does not itself prove stronger delivery.
The notice says the system could be used, not that it changed decisions or results.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 Turkish nuclear command-and-control or custody evidence is absent; the dossier mostly shows inherited treaty/NATO/IAEA posture plus civil-nuclear and mediation choices.
Direct forensic or documentary proof of Erdoğan's own assets, beneficial ownership, or personal enrichment in 2022 is still missing.
Independent corroboration beyond Reuters-style reporting is still thin for the media-control and family-access claims.
Audit-grade verification of project delivery and personnel effects is still thin; the package leans heavily on official program documents and self-reported completion counts.
